findings.evidence: Scaling.lean:74-76 `have hmem := Submodule.smul_mem (1 : Submodule ℤ ℚ) n (L.form_mem_one ...)` / `simpa only [LinearMap.smul_apply, Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul] using hmem`, repeated at 262-263 and 289-290; `form_mem_one` is TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/IntegralLattice/Basic.lean:89, `le_dual` is the structure field at Basic.lean:69.
findings.fix: In `smul_ofSubmodule` replace the inline `by`-block with `(n • ofSubmodule S B hB hle).le_dual` (that term's carrier is `S` and form is `(n : ℚ) • B` by `rfl`, so the type matches exactly). In `smul_ofBasis` use `fun i j ↦ (n • ofBasis b B hB hint).form_mem_one ⟨b i, Submodule.subset_span ⟨i, rfl⟩⟩ ⟨b j, Submodule.subset_span ⟨j, rfl⟩⟩`. For the two `neg_*` obligations factor the single step out once, e.g. `theorem intCast_mul_mem_one (n : ℤ) {q : ℚ} (hq : q ∈ (1 : Submodule ℤ ℚ)) : (n : ℚ) * q ∈ (1 : Submodule ℤ ℚ)`, and call it at all five sites.
findings.issue: The integrality-preservation argument (`Submodule.smul_mem (1 : Submodule ℤ ℚ) n ... ; simpa only [LinearMap.smul_apply, Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul]`) is written out five times: `scale`'s `le_dual` field (lines 70-76), `smul_ofSubmodule` (258-263), `smul_ofBasis` (288-290), and the `Submodule.neg_mem` variants in `neg_ofSubmodule` (270-275) and `neg_ofBasis` (298-300). The `smul_ofSubmodule` hypothesis is literally the `le_dual` field of the term already built by `scale`.

findings.evidence: `protected theorem map_smulₛₗ [SMul R α] [SMul S β] (f : α → β) (σ : R → S) (r : R) (hf : ∀ a, f (r • a) = σ r • f a) (M : Matrix m n α) : (r • M).map f = σ r • M.map f` — mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Defs.lean:369.
findings.fix: Replace with the library lemma: `have hmap := Matrix.map_smulₛₗ (algebraMap ℤ ℚ) (Int.cast) n (fun a ↦ by push_cast [smul_eq_mul]; ring) G`, whose conclusion is exactly `(n • G).map (algebraMap ℤ ℚ) = (n : ℚ) • G.map (algebraMap ℤ ℚ)`.
findings.issue: The `hmap` step in `smul_ofGramMatrix` re-derives `Matrix.map_smulₛₗ` by hand (`ext i j; simp only [Matrix.map_apply, Matrix.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, map_mul]; rfl`).

findings.evidence: Scaling.lean:239-240 docstring: "simplification already derives it from `neg_form` and the corresponding bilinear-form result"; `grep -rn "nondegenerate_neg_iff" TauCeti/` returns only the two definitions and the module-docstring lines, no use sites.
findings.fix: Delete `IntegralLattice.nondegenerate_neg_iff`; callers get the statement from `simp` via `neg_form` and `TauCeti.BilinForm.nondegenerate_neg_iff`. (`nondegenerate_smul_iff` at line 162 earns its place: its `IsRegular ((n : ℚ))` side condition is not simp-dischargeable from `n ≠ 0`.)
findings.issue: `IntegralLattice.nondegenerate_neg_iff` duplicates the composition of two `@[simp]` lemmas added in this same PR: `neg_form` (Scaling.lean:192) rewrites `(-L).form` to `-L.form`, and `TauCeti.BilinForm.nondegenerate_neg_iff` (BilinearForm/Basic.lean:73) closes the result. Its own docstring states this, and grep shows no consumer anywhere in the repo.

findings.evidence: Scaling.lean:194-195, 280-281, 305-306 are character-for-character the same two tactic lines modulo the form variable (`L.form` vs `B`).
findings.fix: State it once, e.g. `theorem intCast_neg_one_smul (B : LinearMap.BilinForm ℚ V) : ((-1 : ℤ) : ℚ) • B = -B`, and `rw` it in all three proofs (or, in the two constructor lemmas, `rw [← neg_form]` after `smul_ofSubmodule`/`smul_ofBasis` to reuse `neg_form` directly).
findings.issue: The cast computation `((-1 : ℤ) : ℚ) • B = -B` is proved three times by the identical two-line block `norm_num only [Int.cast_neg, Int.cast_one]; exact neg_one_smul ℚ B`: in `neg_form` (194-195), `neg_ofSubmodule` (280-281), and `neg_ofBasis` (305-306).

summary: The lattice-level material is new (no `IntegralLattice` in Mathlib) and reuses `Matrix.det_smul`, `Submodule.smul_mem` and `IsSymm.smul`/`.neg` correctly, but the integrality argument is copied verbatim across five declarations, one Gram-matrix step re-derives `Matrix.map_smulₛₗ`, and `nondegenerate_neg_iff` restates what its component simp lemmas already prove.
